scenario: Summit ridge. 20 mph wind, 25°F, and it just started to sleet.
Top is 0.4 miles. Your gloves are soaked.
realityCheck: Wet gloves at 25 degrees in wind are a frostnip setup within the hour. The summit is 0.4 miles; your hands are the whole trip home.
headline: Sleet. Soaked gloves. 0.4 to go.
caption:
The top is right there. So is the sleet.

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Out and back, 6 miles each way. You're at the turnaround.
A loop option adds 2 miles but you've never run it and it's 4:40pm.
headline: New loop. 25 minutes of daylight.
caption:
Known trail or new loop in the dark?

Comment LOOP or BACK.

scenario: Last descent of the day. Wet roots, wet rock, 2 miles of it.
Your brakes started squealing on the climb.
headline: Wet roots. Squealing brakes.
caption:
Roll it or walk it?

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Stream crossing, ankle deep, ice on both banks.
You have waterproof boots and one pair of dry socks for 3 more days.
headline: Ice on the banks. One dry pair.
caption:
Trust the boots or trust your toes?

Comment BOOTS or BARE.

scenario: It's rifle season. You hear shots across the valley, maybe half a mile off.
You're in gray and green. The car is 5 miles the other way.
realityCheck: Hunters are usually careful, but gray and green in rifle season is on you. Blaze orange, loud voices and open ground beat hoping.
headline: Rifle season. Gray jacket.
caption:
Shots across the valley. You're not wearing orange.

Comment GO or BACK.

scenario: Multipitch, 38°F in the shade. Your fingers stopped feeling the holds a pitch ago.
Two pitches left, both in the sun. Rapping now takes an hour.
headline: Numb fingers. Sun two pitches up.
caption:
Climb toward the sun or rap into the shade?

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Snow covered the trail an hour ago. No tracks ahead of you.
A drainage below looks like it leads to the road. Your map shows cliffs between.
realityCheck: Drainages pull people off trail and over cliffs every winter. Your own tracks are the one route you know goes.
headline: Snow erased the trail.
caption:
Down the drainage or back the way you came?

Comment DRAIN or BACK.

scenario: Resort opens tomorrow. Tonight the lifts are off and the ropes are up.
Fresh snow, a headlamp, and a skin track someone already set.
headline: Closed resort. Fresh snow. Headlamp.
caption:
Earn it tonight or wait for the chairs?

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: 28°F at the start, 50°F by noon. 18 mile loop.
Pack the shell and sweat, or leave it and gamble.
headline: 28 at the start. 50 by noon.
caption:
Carry the shell for four hours you might not need it?

Comment PACK or LEAVE.
realityCheck: Cold starts turn into warm finishes most days in shoulder season. The shell matters for the day the forecast is wrong, and that day doesn't announce itself.

scenario: Class 3 ridge. A thin glaze of ice on the north side of every hold.
Summit is 300 ft up. The sun hits it in 40 minutes.
realityCheck: Verglas on class 3 turns a scramble into a fall. Forty minutes of waiting is cheap insurance.
headline: Verglas. Sun in 40 minutes.
caption:
Go now on ice, or wait for the sun?

Comment NOW or WAIT.

scenario: Last river day of the year. Water is 42°F. You have a wetsuit, not a drysuit.
The rapid ahead is one you've swum before.
realityCheck: A swim in 42 degree water in a wetsuit gives you minutes of useful movement, not many. The portage trail exists for exactly this day.
headline: 42 degree water. A rapid you've swum.
caption:
Run it or walk it?

Comment RUN or PORTAGE.
